overview: The Northwest Ice Couloir splits the northwest face of Eldorado above the wild Marble Creek Cirque, offering 2-3 long pitches (often simul-climbed) up the couloir to a flat shoulder just below the summit's famous knife-edge ridge — a steeper, more technical alternative to the standard East Ridge, reached via a long and fairly complex glaciated traverse around the mountain.

face: Upper South Face (crux traverse), below the summit block
overview: A rock alternative to the adjacent Terrible Traverse, encountered above the South Chute around 7,400-7,450 ft. Climbers cross an airy, narrow ledge with thin footholds by jamming fingers into a continuous horizontal crack/flake that runs the length of the traverse, giving good hands even though the feet are marginal. Because it doesn't depend on snow conditions, many parties prefer it over the Terrible Traverse once it's dry.
beta: On the standard South Chute approach, the Finger Traverse is crossed on the way to the summit and again on the descent. From the summit ridge near the Terrible Traverse, locate the downsloping ledge on the eastern side. Place your fingers in the horizontal crack running along the top edge and traverse carefully. The slab below is steep and exposure is extreme—a fall would be fatal. The traverse exits to easier terrain and rejoins the descent route.

overview: This is the standard finish on the highest summit in the Olympics, reached after one of the longest approaches in the Lower 48. After miles of rainforest and a glacier crossing, the climb tops out by winding up a series of loose ramps on the east face of the summit pinnacle. The moves are moderate, but the rock is rotten and an exposed corner is best protected — a small, serious finale to a big wilderness peak.

From Snow Dome, ascend toward Crystal Pass at 7,250 feet. After crossing Crystal Pass and traversing Five Fingers Ridge, encounter the false summit before the final push. overview: Mount Stone is a high-prominence, triple-summited peak (South/main summit 6,612 ft, plus Middle ~6,600 ft and North ~6,400 ft summits) above Lake of the Angels in the southeastern Olympic Mountains. It is the highest point in Mason County. The lower approach lies in the Mount Skokomish Wilderness (Olympic National Forest); the upper basin, lake, and summit sit just inside the Olympic National Park boundary. beta: From Hamma Hamma River Road, hike the steep Putvin Trail (FST 813) through Olympic National Forest gaining nearly 3,000 feet in less than 4 miles. route: Putvin Trail / Lake of the Angels Scramble
overview: The standard route up Mount Stone, the highest point in Mason County. From the Putvin Trail and Lake of the Angels, a class 3 rock scramble of roughly 5,000 ft of gain over about 10 miles round trip gains the summit, with broad views of The Brothers, Mount Anderson, Mount Deception, Mount Constance, and Mount Olympus.
beta: Putvin Trail is notorious for its steep pitch, gaining nearly 3,000 feet in less than 4 miles. The trail negotiates several short sections of Class 3 scrambling over wet rocks and tree roots before reaching the Lake of the Angels basin. This route is more direct than any traverse and is the most commonly used summer climbing route on Mount Stone.
